inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: More tenancies don’t mean much if people are still being pushed out of their homes. Rising eviction notices, homelessness and emergency accommodation expose a housing system that manages insecurity instead of guaranteeing people a stable place to live. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 should be judged by whether they deliver real security—especially for renters most at risk of displacement—not by headline figures that make a deepening crisis look solved. Renter protection must come before appearances.
